sentinels.purpose: The freshly generated plaintext auditor password (synthetic run): must occur ZERO times in every PostgreSQL log line, in pg_stat_statements, in every driver-recorded statement text, bind value and connection option, and in tool output. PLAINTEXT_NOT_PRESENT is the gating property.
The SCRAM-SHA-256 verifier derived from it: counted separately (DERIVED_MATERIAL_PRESENT is measured and classified, never merged with PLAINTEXT_NOT_PRESENT).
Carried from v1.0.0: the operator connection string appears only in the tool's environment block (PEB), now bound to process identity (pid + creation time).

positive_controls.description: The SCRAM-SHA-256 derivation reproduces the RFC 7677 test exchange (ClientProof and ServerSignature byte-exact) and emits PostgreSQL's verifier format SCRAM-SHA-256$<iter>:<salt>$<StoredKey>:<ServerKey>.

Disposable PostgreSQL (supabase/postgres:17.6.1.159): the real outside mint tool installs a verifier; pg_authid holds exactly a valid SCRAM verifier; authentication with the original plaintext succeeds.

The mint harness: the only password-related value sent is a verifier that verifies against the plaintext handed to the depositor; the plaintext appears in no driver event, bind value or connection option.

OEP-1 v2 evaluates PLAINTEXT_NOT_SERVER_VISIBLE, TARGET_SESSION_BOUND, STARTUP_PARAMETERS_CLOSED, TOOL_HASH_BOUND and PROBE_MINT_CONFIGURATION_COHERENT separately, with DERIVED_MATERIAL_EXPOSURE classified apart and non-gating for plaintext.
The PEB observer binds each observation to (pid, creation time); the author demonstration is repeated and reported with its pass count.

negative_controls.description: With log_parser_stats, log_lock_waits (+ a real lock wait on pg_authid), startup GUC injection and a pg_tle passcheck hook ALL enabled, plus log_statement=all with parameters, debug_print_*, auto_explain nested at 0 ms, pg_stat_statements track=all and pgaudit where available, the synthetic plaintext occurs ZERO times in the PostgreSQL logs and pg_stat_statements; the same pressure on the OLD route-B statements reproduces the leak (control that the pressure works).
After installation a wrong plaintext fails authentication; the verifier string itself used as a password fails authentication.
The DO block refuses (D1_VERIFIER_REQUIRED) a value that is not a SCRAM verifier, so a plaintext can never be stored or passed to a password-check hook through this statement.

An operator URL with any query parameter or fragment, another database, another port, or a host that only shares a prefix/suffix with the planned host is refused by the launcher and by both tools before any driver call.
OEP-1 evidence whose recorded and recomputed verdicts are both a non-PASS is NOT accepted by PMR-14.
The mint plan's validUntil is the effective N09, never N08 (with synthetic closed OEP-1 evidence).
A dirty worktree makes the gate STOP (STOP_DIRTY), exercised through the gate's evaluation function.
When N04 is NOT_SATISFIED no plan is derived.
The launcher run leaves the REAL process.env without the operator variable (not only the injected env).
The tool environment allowlist is asserted against a literal, not against the constant under test.
Two processes with the same pid and different creation times are two observations; a clean process's name never labels a leaking one that reused its pid.
The gate refuses to plan the probe unless a terminal-PASS certification event certifies an ancestor candidate carrying the same channel binding.
A driver whose files differ from the pinned driver digest is refused (not only by version).

mutation_controls.description: PMR-14 stops requiring a PASS verdict -> R2-N-E1 RED.
Host comparison by startsWith -> R2-N-STARTUP RED.
validUntil derived from N08 -> R2-N-P1 RED.
SCRAM derivation altered (wrong key label / iteration) -> R2-P-1 RED.
Observation keyed by pid alone -> R2-N-PID-REUSE RED.
A comment-only mutant must survive; kills are attributed only to tests outside the pin block.
